content:
The outside world generally expects Apple to launch a brand new iPad mini equipped with an OLED screen before the end of this month. Today, an unverified new rumour once again claims that the new iPad mini will switch to an OLED screen, but will still only have a 60Hz refresh rate and will not support ProMotion.

The OLED version of the iPad mini may not support ProMotion

This is already the second time we have heard this rumour, but both times it comes from the same source: the yeux1122 account on Naver. That account has a very mixed track record when it comes to Apple rumours, and often seems to merely relay information from anonymous sources rather than providing its own exclusive scoops.

Even so, yeux1122's latest post claims that some "overseas sources" mentioned the new OLED iPad mini would have 120Hz, though "domestic production scale has been confirmed" to use a 60Hz screen.

Let me stress once again that I harbour considerable scepticism about this rumour, as no other reliable sources have corroborated it.

That said, if true, this would disappoint iPad mini buyers. The iPad mini upgrade is expected to bring a number of other notable improvements, including:

  • An OLED display.
  • An upgrade to the Apple A20 Pro chip, a step up from the A17 Pro chip currently used in the iPad mini.
  • A redesigned exterior with slimmer bezels, and possibly improved water resistance.
  • The front-facing FaceTime camera will move to the landscape edge, in line with Apple's other iPad models.

If Apple makes all of these changes yet stops short of upgrading the display to 120Hz ProMotion, it would significantly take the shine off the launch of the new iPad mini.

The new iPad mini is expected to launch at the end of this month, so we won't have to wait long to find out.

What do you think? Will the new iPad mini come with ProMotion and a 120Hz refresh rate? Let us know in the comments section.
